paragraphs.source_en: “Ah, enough. That is your opinion... I have my own plans.” The lady smiled forlornly and turned her gaze toward the courtyard.

paragraphs.source_en: “Surely my thinking cannot be wrong.” As Hidetada murmured this to himself, Lady Asahi suddenly bent forward and burst into tears. The maid seated beside her at the end of the row started in surprise. Gradually, her shrill crying subsided into sobs.

paragraphs.source_zh: “我的想法应该不会错。”在秀忠自言自语的当儿，朝日夫人突然弯腰哭了出来。并排坐在末席的侍女吃了一惊。渐渐地，尖声的哭泣变成了呜咽。

paragraphs.source_en: With her head bowed, the lady said, “Ah, you are still young. You have not endured the torment and blows that I have... Forgive your mother for making such tiresome complaints.”

paragraphs.source_en: “No, no, I understand how you feel, Mother...” Hidetada could say no more. He had meant to say that he understood the lady well, but that would have been a lie. Hidetada had no idea at all why she was so deeply agitated.

paragraphs.source_en: Lady Asahi wiped her eyes, but fresh tears spilled forth despite her efforts. These were the lonely sobs welling from the depths of a woman’s heart—a woman with neither husband nor child.
